title_en: Which matter arises from which origin (past action, mind, temperature, nutriment)

summary_en: Both sources sort the twenty-eight kinds of matter by how many of the four origins can produce them. The four origins are past action (kamma), mind, temperature and nutriment. Nine kinds can arise from all four: the eight 'inseparable' kinds (earth, water, fire, air, colour, smell, taste, nutritive essence) plus the space between groups. Three kinds (lightness, softness, workability) arise from mind, temperature and nutriment. Sound arises from mind (speech) and temperature (such as the noise of wind). Nine kinds arise only from past action: the five sense-sensitivities, the two kinds of sex-matter, the life-faculty and the heart-base. Two kinds arise only from mind: bodily and vocal intimation. The four characteristics (growth, continuity, decay, impermanence) arise from none, because they are only features of other matter. Totalled by origin, this gives 18 kinds of kamma-born matter, 15 mind-born, 13 temperature-born and 12 nutriment-born. The Margaya adds that lightness and the rest appear only when mind, weather and food are good, and that by strict reasoning space arises from no condition.

sinhala_explanation.heading: ප්‍රත්‍යය ගණන අනුව රූප බෙදීම
sinhala_explanation.text: රූපයන් අතර එක් ප්‍රත්‍යයකින්, දෙකකින්, තුනකින්, සතරකින් හට ගන්නා රූප ද, කිසිම ප්‍රත්‍යයකින් හට නොගන්නා රූප ද ඇත [C069-M:L3]. (1) කම්ම, ඍතු, චිත්ත, ආහාර යන සතරින්ම උපදින රූප නවයකි: පඨවි, ආපෝ, තේජෝ, වායෝ, වර්ණ, ගන්ධ, රස, ඕජා සහ පරිච්ඡේද රූපය [C069-P:L16–L24; C069-M:L13]. (2) චිත්ත, ඍතු, ආහාර යන තුනෙන් උපදින්නේ ලහුතා, මුදුතා, කම්මඤ්ඤතා යන තුනයි [C069-P:L26–L30; C069-M:L11]. (3) චිත්ත, ඍතු යන දෙකෙන් උපදින්නේ ශබ්ද රූපය පමණි [C069-P:L32]; මාර්ගයට අනුව කතා කරන ශබ්දය චිත්තජ ය, සුළං හැමීම ආදියෙන් හටගන්නා ශබ්දය ඍතුජ ය [C069-M:L9]. (4) එක් ප්‍රත්‍යයකින් පමණක් උපදින රූප එකොළොසකි: කර්මයෙන් පමණක් චක්ඛු, සෝත, ඝාණ, ජිව්හා, කාය ප්‍රසාද, ස්ත්‍රීභාව, පුරුෂභාව, හදය රූපය, ජීවිතේන්ද්‍රිය යන නවය [C069-P:L34–L42; C069-M:L5]; චිත්තයෙන් පමණක් කාය විඤ්ඤත්ති, වචී විඤ්ඤත්ති යන දෙක [C069-P:L46–L49; C069-M:L7]. (5) කිසිම ප්‍රත්‍යයකින් නූපදින්නේ උපචය, සන්තති, ජරතා, අනිච්චතා යන සතරයි [C069-P:L51–L56].

sinhala_explanation.heading: ලක්ෂණ රූප සහ ආකාශ ධාතුව: විශේෂ අවස්ථා දෙක
sinhala_explanation.text: ලක්ෂණ රූප සතර අනෙක් රූපයන්ගේ ලක්ෂණ බැවින් 'මේ ප්‍රත්‍යයෙන් උපන්නේ' යයි කිව නොහැකි බව ප්‍රදීපිකාව කියයි [C069-P:L58]. මාර්ගයද ඒවා කර්මාදියෙන් හටගන්නා රූපයන්ගේ ඉපදීම, දිරීම, බිඳීම යන ලක්ෂණ මාත්‍රයක් බැවින් ප්‍රත්‍යයෙන් නොහටගන්නා ලෙස දක්වයි; නමුත් උපචය, සන්තති දෙක කර්මාදි ප්‍රත්‍යයෙන් හටගන්නා රූප ලෙස අටුවාවල දක්වා ඇති බවද සඳහන් කරයි [C069-M:L15]. ආකාශ ධාතුව ගැන මාර්ගය මෙසේ පැහැදිලි කරයි: ඉතා කුඩා යැයි සලකන පරමාණුවේ ද බොහෝ රූප කලාප ඇති අතර ඒවා අතර වෙන් කරන ආකාශයක් ද ඇත. තදින්ම කිවහොත් ආකාශ ධාතුව කිසිම ප්‍රත්‍යයකින් නොහටගන්නා දෙයකි; එහෙත් කර්මාදියෙන් හටගත් කලාප වෙන් කරමින් ඒවා අතර පවතින ආකාශයත් ඒ ඒ ප්‍රත්‍යයෙන්ම හටගත් රූපයක් ලෙස ගණන් ගැනීමෙන් එය සතර ප්‍රත්‍යයෙන්ම හටගන්නා රූපයක් ලෙස කියනු ලැබේ [C069-M:L13].

sinhala_explanation.heading: ලහුතාදි තුන: හොඳ සිත, හොඳ කාලගුණය, හොඳ ආහාරය
sinhala_explanation.text: මාර්ගයට අනුව ලහුතා, මුදුතා, කම්මඤ්ඤතා හටගන්නේ හොඳ චිත්ත, ඍතු, ආහාරවලිනි. කාලගුණය නරක් වූ විට, සිත නරක් වූ විට, නොමනා ආහාරයෙන් හටගන්නා කලාපවල ලහුතාදි තුන නොලැබේ. ලහුතාදියෙන් යුත් කලාප නැති විට ශරීරය බරව, තදව, ක්‍රියාවට නුසුදුසුව පවතී [C069-M:L11].

sinhala_explanation.heading: ප්‍රත්‍යය අනුව එකතුව: කර්මජ 18, චිත්තජ 15, ඍතුජ 13, ආහාරජ 12
sinhala_explanation.text: කර්මජ රූප අටළොසකි: ඉන් නවයක් ඒකාන්ත කර්මජ ය (වෙනත් ප්‍රත්‍යයකින් ඉපදවිය නොහැක): ප්‍රසාද පස, භාව දෙක, ජීවිතේන්ද්‍රිය, හදය වස්තුව; ඉතිරි නවය (අවිනිබ්භෝග අට හා පරිච්ඡේද රූපය) අනේකාන්ත ය, මන්ද අන්‍ය ප්‍රත්‍යයෙන්ද ඉපදවිය හැකි බැවිනි [C069-P:L60–L72; C069-M:L17]. චිත්තජ රූප පසළොසකි: ඒකාන්ත චිත්තජ විඤ්ඤත්ති දෙක, සහ අනේකාන්ත තෙළෙස (අවිනිබ්භෝග අට, පරිච්ඡේද රූපය, ශබ්දය, විකාර රූප තුන) [C069-P:L76–L84; C069-M:L19]. ඍතුජ රූප තෙළෙසකි: අවිනිබ්භෝග අට, පරිච්ඡේද රූපය, ශබ්දය, විකාර තුන [C069-P:L86–L94; C069-M:L21]. ආහාරජ රූප දොළොසකි: අවිනිබ්භෝග අට, පරිච්ඡේද රූපය, විකාර තුන [C069-P:L96–L103; C069-M:L23]. සියල්ල එකතු කළ විට 9 + 3 + 1 + 11 + 4 = 28 වේ [C069-P:L16–L56].

key_terms.en: origin or condition that produces matter
matter produced by past intentional action
exclusively from one origin / from that origin among others
the eight inseparables: earth, water, fire, air, colour, smell, taste, nutritive essence
the eight faculty-kinds: five sense-sensitivities, two sex-kinds, life-faculty
key_terms.note: Used by M [C069-M:L5]; not spelled out in M

key_terms.en: characteristics of matter; from no origin

key_terms.note: Cited by M for a divergent view [C069-M:L15]

human_interpretation_en.heading: Four hands shape the body
human_interpretation_en.text: The source names four forces that are always building the body. One is what you have done in the past, which the tradition says shaped what you were born with. The others are your present mind, the weather and warmth around and inside you, and the food you eat. This list sorts out which parts of you each force can reach. Some things, like the eye's ability to see or whether you were born male or female, come only from the past and cannot be produced by today's food or mood. Others, like how light or heavy your body feels, respond to the present: to your state of mind, the season and your last meal.

human_interpretation_en.heading: What the present can and cannot touch
human_interpretation_en.text: For a film series about vulnerability, the useful edge here is the split between what can be tended and what was handed to us. A person can eat better, keep warm, calm their mind, and the body's ease will answer. But the basic equipment, such as the senses, the life in the body and its sex, is outside the reach of present effort in this account. The honest human feeling is a mix of agency and helplessness. There is a lot we can do for our bodies, and a core we did not choose.

human_interpretation_en.heading: Two kinds of sound
human_interpretation_en.text: The Margaya's small example is worth keeping. A voice speaking and the wind in the trees are both sound, but one comes from a mind that means something and the other only from weather. A place where both can be heard at once, a voice calling over a gale, holds the distinction without anyone having to explain it.

does_not_transfer: 'Your body is your karma' or 'illness and disability are punishment': the source says certain kinds of matter are produced by past action. It does not license judging any person's body, disability or sex as deserved, and the films must never imply that.
'Mind over matter': the mind produces some matter (movement, speech, some lightness), but the sense organs, the life-faculty and the heart-base are outside its reach in this scheme.
'You are what you eat': nutriment produces twelve kinds of matter but not the senses, sex, life or the capacity to speak.
'Temperature' (utu) here means the heat element as a producing condition, both inside and outside the body. It is not simply 'the weather' or a climate-science claim.

story_seeds.seed: A village runner training for a national meet on the food, weather and mood available to them
story_seeds.what_camera_could_observe: Dawn training on dirt roads, meals at home, a day of heat that slows them, race-day nerves, what the body does well and what it simply cannot
story_seeds.why_it_fits: Lightness and readiness respond to food, weather and mind [C069-M:L11]. The underlying capacities are given rather than made by training.
story_seeds.setting_type: rural school and its surrounding roads
story_seeds.risk: It could become an underdog sports story with the doctrine attached. Poverty should not be turned into a spectacle.

story_seeds.seed: A fish auction on a windy beach where auctioneers' calls compete with wind and surf
story_seeds.what_camera_could_observe: Shouted bids, gestures, waves and gusts drowning words, buyers leaning in to hear
story_seeds.why_it_fits: Speech is mind-born sound and wind-noise is temperature-born sound [C069-M:L9]. Gesture (bodily intimation) comes only from mind [C069-M:L7].
story_seeds.risk: Low. The danger is only that it stays a sound-design exercise with no human stake.

story_seeds.seed: A Kandyan dance student preparing for a graded exam
story_seeds.what_camera_could_observe: Practice, the teacher correcting posture, a day the body feels heavy, a day it flows, exam-day nerves
story_seeds.why_it_fits: Movement is driven by mind [C069-P:L46–L49], and the ease or heaviness of the body shifts with mind, weather and food [C069-M:L11].
story_seeds.risk: The student could be framed as an illustration of 'mind moves body'. Their own ambitions must lead, and minors need guardian consent.

story_seeds.seed: Families in the hill country through the cold, wet monsoon months
story_seeds.what_camera_could_observe: Damp clothes, fires kept going, stiff joints in the morning, warm food, children and elders adapting differently
story_seeds.why_it_fits: Temperature produces thirteen kinds of matter, including the body's lightness and pliancy [C069-P:L86–L94]. Warmth and cold visibly shape how bodies feel and move.
story_seeds.risk: Hardship could be aestheticised as moody weather. Housing and health realities should not be glossed over.

cross_source_notes: The lists and totals (18 / 15 / 13 / 12) are identical in both sources [C069-P:L60–L103; C069-M:L17–L23].

On the characteristics: the Pradeepika states flatly that they arise from no condition because they are only characteristics [C069-P:L58]. The Margaya agrees but adds that the commentaries treat growth and continuity as produced by kamma and the other conditions [C069-M:L15].

On space: the Pradeepika lists it among the nine four-origin kinds without comment [C069-P:L24]. The Margaya explains that strictly it has no origin and is counted with its groups only by convention [C069-M:L13].
On the lightness triad: the Pradeepika gives only the list [C069-P:L26–L30]. The Margaya explains that it arises only from good mind, weather and food and is missing when these are bad [C069-M:L11].
The Pradeepika tabulates exclusive and non-exclusive kinds for kamma and mind [C069-P:L60–L84]. The Margaya uses the collective term 'eight faculty-kinds' instead of listing them [C069-M:L5].
uncertainties: The Pradeepika extract is lists only. Its scope note says the explanation of how each origin produces matter was cut into Concept 68 [C069-P:L9], which was not read for this digest. The mechanism is therefore not covered here.

C069-M:L11 reads 'සෘතුව නරක් වූ කල්හි හටගන්නා චිත්තජ රූපයන්හි ද, සිත නරක් වූ කල්හි හට ගන්නා චිත්තජ රූපවල ද'. The first 'චිත්තජ' probably should be 'සෘතුජ' (temperature-born). It has not been corrected, and the reading needs an expert check.
C069-P:L16 lists the four conditions as 'කම්ම, ඍතු, චිත්ත, ආහාර', while elsewhere the order is kamma, mind, temperature, nutriment. This probably has no significance.
C069-P:L107 refers to a chart on p. 129 of the book, which is not in the extract.
The commentarial view cited in C069-M:L15 (growth and continuity have origins) is reported second-hand. Which commentary is meant is not stated.
